newsitem.title: CHINA: China gives Comoros president red carpet treatment.
newsitem.headline: China gives Comoros president red carpet treatment.

text.p: China, eager to prevent rival Taiwan from wooing away diplomatic allies, has rolled out the red carpet for the visiting president of Comoros -- a tiny African nation with a population of less than one million.

"All nations, regardless of size, wealth and strength, are equal members of the international community," the China Daily on Wednesday quoted Chinese President Jiang Zemin as telling visiting Comoros President Mohamed Taki.
The newspaper splashed on its front page a photograph of Jiang and Taki and gave extensive coverage to the visit.
Jiang was quoted as saying the Chinese government was willing to strengthen and develop sincere friendship and cooperation with the Islamic country.
China and Comoros signed a new agreement on Tuesday with the host country pledging to provide economic and technical support, the newspaper said. It did not give details.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. China considers Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation.
China has scornfully accused Taiwan of practising "dollar diplomacy" -- using its wealth to buy diplomatic allies.

Beijing scored a major diplomatic victory over its rival last month when South African President Nelson Mandela announced that Pretoria would cut diplomatic ties with Taiwan and forge full diplomatic links with China by the end of 1997.
